filters.name: Select Edges by Expression
filters.shortDescription: Selects polyline edges for which a boolean expression evaluates true.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Boolean function using muparser lib to select the **real edges of a polyline layer** — the kind produced by the *Create Polyline* filters — not the sides of triangles.

Endpoint values use the same names as the first two corners of a face: `x0,y0,z0`/`x1,y1,z1`, `nx0`..`nz1`, `r0,g0,b0,a0`/`r1`..`a1`, `q0,q1`, `vi0,vi1`, `vsel0,vsel1`. The edge itself gives `er,eg,eb,ea` (current color), `eq` (scalar), `ei` (index) and `esel`, plus the derived `elen` (length), `emx,emy,emz` (midpoint) and `edx,edy,edz` (unit direction; zero for a degenerate edge). Bounding-box values `xmin`..`bbdiag` are available as everywhere else.

parameters.label: Boolean Function
parameters.help: Boolean expression evaluated per edge.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Seed for the `rnd()` and `randInt()` helpers, which only matter if your expression calls them. Zero draws a fresh seed on every run; any other value makes the expression exactly reproducible.

filters.shortDescription: Computes per-edge RGBA colors from expressions.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Color function using muparser lib to generate a new RGBA color for every edge of a **polyline layer**. Each edge takes one flat color, which is what distinguishes this from interpolating the endpoint vertex colors — pick *Per-Edge* as the edge color source in the render panel to see it.

Endpoint values use the same names as the first two corners of a face: `x0,y0,z0`/`x1,y1,z1`, `nx0`..`nz1`, `r0,g0,b0,a0`/`r1`..`a1`, `q0,q1`, `vi0,vi1`, `vsel0,vsel1`. The edge itself gives `er,eg,eb,ea` (current color), `eq` (scalar), `ei` (index) and `esel`, plus the derived `elen` (length), `emx,emy,emz` (midpoint) and `edx,edy,edz` (unit direction; zero for a degenerate edge). Bounding-box values `xmin`..`bbdiag` are available as everywhere else.

parameters.help: Expression for red output in range [0, 255].

filters.name: Compute Edge Scalar by Expression
filters.shortDescription: Computes a per-edge scalar from an expression.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Scalar function using muparser lib to write one value per edge of a **polyline layer**. Feed the result to *Colorize Edges by Scalar*, or tick *Map into Color* here to do both in one step.

Edge scalars survive a PLY round trip as a `quality` property on the edge element; tick *Edge Scalar* in the save dialog to keep them.

Endpoint values use the same names as the first two corners of a face: `x0,y0,z0`/`x1,y1,z1`, `nx0`..`nz1`, `r0,g0,b0,a0`/`r1`..`a1`, `q0,q1`, `vi0,vi1`, `vsel0,vsel1`. The edge itself gives `er,eg,eb,ea` (current color), `eq` (scalar), `ei` (index) and `esel`, plus the derived `elen` (length), `emx,emy,emz` (midpoint) and `edx,edy,edz` (unit direction; zero for a degenerate edge). Bounding-box values `xmin`..`bbdiag` are available as everywhere else.

parameters.label: Scalar Function
parameters.help: Expression evaluated per edge; its value becomes the edge scalar.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.help: Rescale the computed values into [0, 1] once every edge has been evaluated.

parameters.label: Map into Color
parameters.help: Also map the resulting scalar into per-edge color, using the full value range.

parameters.label: Only On Selection
parameters.help: If enabled, the filter affects only selected edges.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Seed for the `rnd()` and `randInt()` helpers, which only matter if your expression calls them. Zero draws a fresh seed on every run; any other value makes the expression exactly reproducible.

filters.name: Create Grid
filters.shortDescription: Creates a regular grid of quads: a plane, subdivided, in any orientation.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Creates a new layer holding a regular grid of quads: a **plane** cut into `Vertices U` × `Vertices V` samples, which is the usual starting point for a ground plane, a cutting plane, a backdrop, or a height field to displace.

The two in-plane directions are called **U** and **V** rather than X and Y, because the grid no longer has to lie in the XY plane: **Normal** turns it to face any direction, and U and V are then whatever two perpendicular directions come with it.

**Fit to Layer** sizes and places the grid from an existing layer instead of from the size boxes: the grid is made as wide as that layer's bounding-box diagonal, square, and centred on the box centre, so it always cuts clean through the object whichever way it is turned. The layer's own transformation is taken into account. Leave it on *None* to use the sizes below.

Without a fit layer, **Center on Origin** decides whether the grid straddles the origin or starts there and runs out along +U and +V.

parameters.label: Vertices U
parameters.help: Number of vertices along the first in-plane direction.

parameters.label: Vertices V
parameters.help: Number of vertices along the second in-plane direction.

parameters.label: Size U
parameters.help: Total extent of the grid along U. Ignored when a fit layer is chosen.

parameters.label: Size V
parameters.help: Total extent of the grid along V. Ignored when a fit layer is chosen.

parameters.label: Normal
parameters.help: Direction the grid faces. U and V are two perpendicular directions in the plane at right angles to it. Need not be normalized.

parameters.label: Fit to Layer
parameters.help: Size the grid as that layer's bounding-box diagonal and centre it on the box centre, taking the layer's transformation into account. None uses the sizes above.

parameters.label: Center on Origin
parameters.help: Straddle the origin instead of starting there and running out along +U and +V. Ignored when a fit layer is chosen, which centres the grid on that layer instead.
